markdown_report:
Select a dependency-isolated, mutation-tested BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter as the first experiment. At 0% progress, reliable measurements offer a stronger foundation than another unverified training intervention.

**Insights from supplied evidence.** (1) All four recent sampler and exported-serving checks passed. The subsequent missing-SciPy failures therefore establish diagnostic execution failures, without establishing serving defects. (2) Recent-item deletion reduced target scores across categories, with Electronics diagnostic hit@10 decreasing by 0.125. These training-prefix interventions motivate recency hypotheses but cannot establish validation gains. (3) Residual probes reported stale prerequisite failures despite successful prerequisites. Availability and gate reasons must therefore derive from current execution state.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Recommender metamorphic testing [1] supports checking input/output relations without exact recommendation labels. Its classical-library results require separate BERT4Rec validation. (2) Mutation assessment [2] motivates deliberately exercising known faults before trusting probes. Detection must exclude equivalent or unexercised mutations. (3) BERT4Rec implementation guidance [3] specifies masked reconstruction and appended-mask serving. These semantics supply concrete fixtures, while positional embeddings prevent assuming arbitrary padding-shift invariance.

The framework groups research into three directions: execution reliability, semantic correctness, and behavioral usefulness.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension |
|---|---|---|
| Execution | Dependency failure; stale gate reasons | Independent probe outcomes |
| Correctness | Passing checkpoint/serving parity | Controlled fault detection |
| Behavior | Recent-deletion effects | Budgeted, serving-aligned audits |

Three atomic ideas follow; scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each out of ten.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Isolate probe execution | 2/8/2 | O: precise adaptation; P: preserves evidence; D: small wrapper | O: standard practice; P: indirect ranking benefit; D: cleanup needs care |
| Mutation-test semantic fixtures [1–3] | 4/8/4 | O: family-specific combination; P: reusable assurance; D: bounded fixtures | O: established technique; P: incomplete fault coverage; D: graph details matter |
| Audit terminal/reconstruction boundary gradients | 5/6/6 | O: specific ranking adaptation; P: objective hypotheses; D: reuses autograd | O: established ingredients; P: local evidence only; D: tied-gradient accounting |

Choose the first two as one diagnostic reliability experiment: isolation supplies valid execution records; mutations assess their detection strength.

```text
save model mode and RNG state
run each probe independently; retain measurements and definitions
derive behavioral gates from current sampler/parity outcomes
exercise one reversible semantic fault at a time
record detection, clean-control alarms, coverage and runtime
restore parameters, hooks, model mode and RNG state
```

Keep one trained BERT4Rec checkpoint per category; mutations are temporary diagnostic interventions. Preserve all adapter interfaces, left-padding semantics, reserved MASK training, appended-mask final-nonpadding readout, routing and predictor consistency. Retain seeds, training limits, data paths and host evaluation. Charge diagnostics to the shared budget; report no validation improvement without host measurements.

idea.description: Build a dependency-isolated, mutation-tested diagnostic adapter for the corrected BERT4Rec baseline, retaining completed measurements when optional probes fail and validating semantic probes against controlled temporary faults.
idea.motivation: The supplied recent results show successful sampler and serialized-serving parity checks followed by missing-SciPy failures in every category. Residual availability reasons contradict the successful prerequisites. Correcting execution and reporting is a feasible early-stage step that makes later model experiments interpretable.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), the actual view.model and every supplied ModelView interface. Propagate the actual category explicitly. Return metrics and metric_definitions with per-probe status, attempted/completed counts, elapsed time and precise failure reasons; unavailable measurements must be null, never zero. Isolate optional imports inside their probes. Replace an optional dependency only with a mathematically equivalent implementation that has been checked on small fixtures; otherwise report that probe unavailable. Distinguish prerequisite failure from execution failure and unsupported architecture. Derive gate reasons after prerequisite execution, and preserve valid completed results even if subsequent probes fail.

Run clean fixtures and one temporary fault at a time: incorrect count-minus-one readout on unequal left-padded histories, omitted appended MASK, disabled padding exclusion with exercised PAD positions, incorrect category routing and altered checkpoint state. Use synthetic fixture histories and valid IDs without accessing held-out labels. Check candidate and batch permutation equivariance, target masking, checkpoint identity and current-model/exported-predictor parity in evaluation mode. Do not assume arbitrary padding shifts preserve scores with absolute positional embeddings. Target leakage fixtures verify the supplied sampler construction; tensors alone cannot prove complete prefix provenance. Use the actual predictor loader and writer rather than inferred source reconstruction.

Report clean-control false alarms and detections among exercised non-equivalent faults, separately by fault; an intentionally changed model need not alter every ranking. Exact checkpoint mismatch is a state-identity failure even when sampled scores happen to agree. Keep temporary mutations in memory and restore state in finally blocks; never deploy mutated checkpoints. Freeze probe rules before examining the mutation results and label subsequent revisions exploratory. These fixtures are diagnostic artifacts, not independently trained models or score fusion.

Keep Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl; preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts remain trial-local and execution single-GPU. Preserve the supplied baseline architecture, sampler and optimizer during this diagnostic experiment. Use exactly one independently trained model/checkpoint per category with reserved-mask supervision and appended-mask inference, reading the actual final nonpadding position. Preserve five real training users per category receiving full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Track all diagnostic cost against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Selection remains the unchanged host macro validation HR@10; no improvement is asserted here.

originality.positive: Combines fault-isolated execution with BERT4Rec-specific semantic fixtures and measured mutation coverage.
originality.negative: Exception isolation, metamorphic testing and mutation assessment are established techniques.

future_potential.positive: Reliable availability and semantic checks can support subsequent sampler, objective and architecture experiments.
future_potential.negative: Diagnostic reliability alone does not establish better recommendations or validation HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: The experiment preserves the trained backbone and serving architecture and can use small deterministic fixtures.
code_difficulty.negative: Fault injection, architecture-aware fixtures, exact restoration and exported-loader verification require careful implementation.
